Blocks lift.call/lift.ret and full §3.7 activation, with b-isa-spec-1a4 for token/classical/region signature source bindings and b-isa-spec-3xe for generic §5.2 state allocation. Do not publish the partial catalog.

title: REF canonical constant bits need an exact integer bit-extraction scalar
description: §11.1 scalar operators are + - * div mod, while the ratified default says bit loops increase from LSB and constants are zero or X of a clean bit. A parameterized N-bit literal C cannot select its i-th bit in that finite scalar grammar: denominator 2^i is not expressible. Repeated quantum increment is semantically correct but introduces non-default MSB increment gates and shared address counters; it must not stand in for canonical constant-bit binding. Surgical repair within the integer parameter grammar: binary prefix [bit,n,i] = floor(n/2^i) mod 2 for nonnegative integers, rejecting negative operands; no angle arithmetic. Add a K row/witness and replace literal/address constants with LSB X leaves, preserving A1 algorithms, schema/envelope/ordinal rules and qxor witness. This parameter-language correction does not choose new interface/class/region descriptor schemas.
close_reason: Resolved by existing §11.1 K23: bit(x,i)=floor(x/2^i) mod 2 for nonnegative integers, no machine-word truncation. conformance/tests/ref_language.rs canonical_integer_literal_has_only_lsb_ordered_x_leaves checks literal 13 emits X at 0,2,3; existing full-domain literal rows and qxor witness unchanged.

Record and decide these host capabilities in ISA 0.9, including names, signatures, states and lifetimes. None is invented in the ISA 0.8 headers.

title: Scheduling ABI leaves request buffer lifetimes and response ownership underspecified
description: ISA 0.8 §11 declares "bennett_status bennett_sched_request_set_object(bennett_sched_request_t*, const uint8_t*, size_t);" and setters for target, params and strings, but never says when their inputs are copied or how long they must remain live. §10 explicitly says "Arguments and the entropy tape are copied at bennett_run; the caller may free its buffers afterwards." No corresponding scheduling statement exists. §11 lists request/response frees and pointer accessors but does not explicitly extend §10 object/pointer lifetime rules to them, specify response independence from the request, required setters/defaults, or status-versus-outcome failures. Define these scheduling call contracts in ISA 0.9. The published header declares only the specified functions and makes no copying/lifetime promises beyond the text.

title: Launch ABI lacks general invalid-argument and allocation-failure contracts
description: ISA 0.8 §10 defines "BENNETT_E_ARG, BENNETT_E_NOMEM" but not general NULL/index validity, output preservation on failure or allocation-failure coverage. It declares status-less accessors such as "uint64_t bennett_result_fault(const bennett_result_t*, size_t i);" and "const uint8_t* bennett_request_payload(const bennett_request_t*, size_t* len);". VM docs/PROGRESS.md requires valid objects/out-length pointers, fails loudly on misuse, maps recoverable argument-vector allocation failure to E_NOMEM, permits allocator aborts elsewhere, and accepts NULL in matching frees. These are VM interpretations, not stated public preconditions. Specify a general failure/precondition contract in ISA 0.9 rather than inventing one in the headers.

title: Launch ABI does not specify host thread synchronization or progress guarantees
description: ISA 0.8 §10 says "bennett_wait blocks until the run leaves RUNNING" and "A run owns the registers and memory it touches exclusively while not CLOSED." These rules do not define thread safety of calls on the same program or whether suspend/reply may run concurrently with wait, nor whether progress is autonomous or cooperative. VM docs/PROGRESS.md chooses cooperative execution and externally synchronized per-program calls. Specify synchronization and progress in ISA 0.9 so host programs can implement wait/suspend safely across providers; do not narrow promised execution capabilities.

title: Effect tape iterator has no specified end-of-tape result
description: ISA 0.8 §10 says "bennett_tape_next yields each effect in tape order" and declares "bennett_status bennett_tape_next(bennett_tape_iter_t*, const char** dev, const char** op, const uint8_t** args, size_t* alen);". Its status enum has no EOF enumerator, and exhaustion, output preservation and repeat calls at EOF have no stated contract. VM docs/PROGRESS.md chooses E_INVALID_STATE, an explicit diagnostic, and untouched outputs. Specify EOF semantics in ISA 0.9 without conflating an implementation convention with normative ABI.

title: Host qreg prepare and measurement bit encoding is unspecified
description: ISA 0.8 §10 declares "bennett_status bennett_qreg_prepare(bennett_program_t*, bennett_qreg, const uint8_t* bits, size_t nbits);" and "bennett_status bennett_result_measurement(const bennett_result_t*, size_t i, bennett_qreg* reg, uint8_t* bits_out, size_t cap, size_t* nbits);". Unlike result_get, neither declaration specifies packed versus byte-per-wire bits, bit order, padding, required cap, or short-buffer output behavior. §3.3 bit 0 to wire 0 does not define the host byte representation. VM docs/PROGRESS.md chooses one byte 0/1 per wire in wire order. Specify interoperable encodings and validation in ISA 0.9; published headers preserve the signatures and do not adopt that VM convention.

title: Publish exact ISA 0.8 launch and scheduling C headers
description: Render accepted ISA sections 10 and 11 in include only; first extend conformance/tests/headers.rs to compile every normative symbol and signature under C11 and C++17. Cite declarations and ownership sentences, file isa-0.9 gaps without inventing ABI, compare read-only VM candidate, run offline conformance, export Beads and commit owned paths without push.
close_reason: Completed: exact launch 0.8 (41 functions, 70 named symbols) and sched 0.8 (15 functions, 21 named symbols) headers; normative inventory tests observed red before implementation and green in C11/C++17. Full offline conformance: 20 passed. All 91 symbol removals, signature/handle mutations and missing C linkage rejected. Six isa-0.9 bugs filed and documented; all 41 VM normative signatures identical, six VM extensions excluded. No spec/interpreter/VM edits or push.

title: ISA 0.8 §4.1: measurement draw ordering unspecified (Born rule only); bennett-vm adopted the reference CLI convention
description: Found by bennett-vm milestone 1 differential harness (bennett-vm 188ab05, docs/PROGRESS.md): §4.1 requires the Born rule but does not say in which order a run's draws are consumed when several measurements occur, so two conformant implementations may differ on --draws inputs. The VM copied the reference CLI's convention to agree. 0.9 should state the draw order (or the draw-consumption rule per measurement) normatively.
notes: Maintainer ratified 2026-10-30 (bennett/docs/decisions/2026-10-30-maintainer-decision-memo.md): state the reference CLI draw-consumption convention normatively in 0.9 §4.1.

comments.author: tobiasosborne
comments.text: Ratified text applied: ed044ec. FIFO draws and bits-lexicographic strict CDF rule in §4.1. Two-measurement witness draws 0.25,0.75 returns bits 01,11 and values 2,3; independent Python/Rust arithmetic and current 0.8 binary agree. SPEC-QUESTIONS 29 closed for 0.9.

title: ISA: lprocs cannot pass tokens or classical args to lifted calls
description: 0.8 §4.2 says tk of lift.oracle_call is a classical argument of the calling oracle, and §3.7 lets an lproc read only its params and locations; draft 0.9 E17.14 makes explicit that lifted-call args are classical arguments of the calling oracle, never locations (a location as a classical arg would be superposed). Consequence: a nested oracle call or a parametrised perm_call made from inside an lproc has no way to obtain a token or classical args. Construction today: inline the call into the oracle body or pass values as in-wires/params instead of args; tokens have no such path. Possible fix: a per-oracle classical-argument environment readable by lprocs (pseudo-locations visible in the closure), or token params for lprocs. Raised by the 0.9 draft job (b-isa-spec-so1) after its review; open question Q14.
close_reason: Q14 applied per 2026-10-29 orchestrator decision and accepted worklog wording: explicit lproc token/classical parameters, complete lifted-call forwarding (including mapped regions), fixed binding instances, charge and identity rules. Draft sections 0.1-0.2, 2, 3.3, 3.6-3.7, 4.2, 4.7-4.8, 5.1, 5.4-5.5, 9.1-9.2, 15, 16.2-16.3 (example 10); spec/isa-0.9.PROGRESS.md Q14 status, derivation and verification updated. Witness row model, JCS/hash cross-checks, diff checks and accepted 0.8 fingerprint/precheck pass. 0.9 executor/hash patching remain at the draft existing gate.

title: ISA 0.8 §17 item 14 contradicts §7.4 on hardware qreg.free
description: §17 item 14 default: an unclean qreg.free on hardware marks the run FAILED with FAULT_UB_TRAP, 'since cleanliness ... is not testable' — a rule conditioned on an untestable fact. §7.4 instead speaks of 'a qreg.free frame whose cleanliness was not verified (hardware, §17 item 14)', i.e. releases proceed unverified. Two implementers could differ (fault every hardware free vs proceed). Draft 0.9 entry K7 reconciles: hardware releases proceed unverified, the frame is marked, uncall and reversal are excluded; a simulator records FAULT_UB_TRAP. Found while drafting 0.9 (b-isa-spec-so1).

title: ISA 0.8 fault 0 produces an unflagged failure despite FAULT_NONE=0
description: Independent evidence review: §4.2/§3.3 permit fault C and lift.faultif p C for any literal C<2^F, including C=0. fault 0 toggles faulted but leaves code=0; §5.2 commits zero payload and XOR 0 into fr, indistinguishable from a successful zero result. This conflicts with NS §4.2 named distinct fault causes and the use of zero fault rate as acceptance. Proposed minimal 0.9 repair keeps the syntax and capability: explicit fault with C=0, or triggered faultif with C=0, uses effective cause FAULT_UB_TRAP=4; forward and inverse fault writes both use that effective cause. Extend the same mapping to proposed CC/R fault. Suite B at B=1 checks target unchanged/fr XOR 4 and prefix clean; B=0 still yields steps code1. No spec edit performed.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — legal fault0 currently commits payload0/code0 and hides failure. Exact 0.9 proposal retains syntax but maps explicit zero cause to existing FAULT_UB_TRAP=4 in forward/inverse and CC/R fault. B=0 yields fr XOR1; B=1 yields fr XOR4; no new fault number. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA 0.8 §3.6: ordering multi-member lproc SCCs is not a total rule
description: Evidence job independently confirms reference-interpreter/SPEC-QUESTIONS.md item 7: §3.6 says lprocs ordered by closure hash with SCC members in SCC index order; member closure hashes are independent digests, so globally sorting member hashes can contradict keeping an SCC in index order. Specify SCC groups ordered by scc_hash for cyclic SCCs (singleton acyclic group key is symbol closure hash), then members by SCC index; retain canonical lift.label values. Add suite F mutual-SCC label vector. Proposed evidence only; spec remains untouched.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: wording-only — order SCC groups by closure-envelope scc_hash (acyclic singleton by closure hash), then members by SCC index, then rows in block order. Add mutual-SCC canonical-label test. No existing example has a multi-member SCC; local hashes unchanged. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: G-16: Stack switching (fibers) and asynchronous interrupts in CC/R
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2b (G-16).

Verdict: New candidate gap.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §3.2 the activation stack is part of the classical environment, not memory; §4.1 has no stack-switch or interrupt mechanism.

Blocks: BLOCKS RUNG 6 unless the Asyncify-style transform plus interrupt polling of dialect O-06 is accepted (large cost, no ISA change). Also affects rung 7 non-local exits (panic) and rung 5 (setjmp-based exceptions, tasks).

Change: CC/R fibers (`fiber.new`, `fiber.switch`, reversed by history), and an interrupt-delivery point tied to device models.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — explicit saved continuations and deterministic polling realise fibers/interrupt modelling on ISA 0.8. Outline ratifies that transform; rungs 5/6/7 need platform implementation and independent comparison, not an ISA fiber opcode. Generic hardware timing equivalence is unverified. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: G-12: Oracle entry state from the caller's run-time classical memory, at native addresses
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2b (G-12).

Verdict: New candidate gap (not in the dialect's list).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §3.7 'Initial allocator state ... storage of mem all zero except global images'; §7.2 'for each interface region ... a base address; all ranges disjoint'; §7.1 one layout for CC and lifted memory, so an interface region can never overlap a CC global or CC heap address.

Blocks: Rung 7 at kernel scale: correct in 0.8 through the replay-plus-copy prologue of dialect O-07, but every oracle invocation pays O(snapshot) steps, each a full memory dispatch, which dominates 7(c). Rung 4 is not affected with the VFS-image design (phase 2 should confirm).

Change: an oracle `mem` slot of kind `overlay` whose region supplies the initial bytes of the globals and heap ranges, plus an allocation-table image (pre-entries for snapshot heap objects, freeable).
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — allocation replay plus snapshot byte copy preserves addresses and restores inputs under prefix reversal. Replay must include dead and zero-sized allocations, not only live objects. Rung 7 runtime-snapshot cost; no rung-4 dependency. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: I5: Done-invariance of idle steps (variable-time readiness; candidate T7)
description:
Source: worklog/001_2026-10-28_bootstrap.md ('Open items (pre-bd issue list)')
Id: I5

State as a property (candidate T7): on a branch that reached HALT at step t, every later forward step is the identity on (ins, tgt, fr, result_val, locations, cells) and leaves its frame at |0>. Make the step variant that controls the successor XOR and both commit exchanges on `not at_HALT` the reference (section 3.6 steps 3-4), add a suite-B test that an idle step is the identity, and add the `pc = HALT` predicate as the 'done' projector in the formal model (section 14). Core.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — identity-idle variant can encode active old_pc as k XOR HALT, reserving zero for idle, without another retained bit. Printed inverse recovers activity from encoded history. 608 small active/idle round trips checked; no demo rung depends on T7. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: I1: Pebbled / checkpointed oracle realisations
description:
Source: worklog/001_2026-10-28_bootstrap.md ('Open items (pre-bd issue list)')
Id: I1

The section 5.2 construction keeps B frames. Bennett-1989 pebbling (and the Knill-1995 strategies in Bennett.jl src/pebble/) trade frames for O(log B) checkpoints at polylog time. T6 arguably admits it as a section 5.7 transformation, but section 11 has no schedule kind to bind or cost a checkpoint and T2 is stated only for the full-history realisation. Spec change: name checkpointed realisations in section 5.7, add a schedule binding and a section 17 default (full history). Core, S1 with default.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — binary pebbling recurrence T(k)=3T(k-1) gives 3^ceil(log2 B) evaluations and O(S log B) checkpoint bits. Polylog-time claim is not established. Exact proposed expansion/resource binding and tests are in the evidence note; 4(c)/7(c) space only. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: I2: Structure recovery of bounded data-dependent loops
description:
Source: worklog/001_2026-10-28_bootstrap.md ('Open items (pre-bd issue list)')
Id: I2

`qloop n while cond` needs `cond` computed before the loop from wires the body does not modify, so a Collatz-style exit cannot use it; the dispatch-free form is `qloop B_iter` with the body predicated on a 'still running' flag. Give that idiom (or a `qloop n until flag` form) in section 4.6 / 5.7 so the specialiser does not pay per-step dispatch over the whole program. Core, S1. (Plan risk R5 notes rung-4 option (c) estimates need this.)
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — structure recovery already permitted by T6; active selectors cannot be modified. Immutable-input prefix selectors or retained history give constructions. Preserving the original row-budget fault boundary is mandatory. Rung 4(c) usefulness depends on implementation proofs. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA: measuring registers wider than 128 bits (efficiency item)
description: measure yields iN with N <= 128 and a view may only be a region-call operand, so a register wider than 128 bits (newly reachable with qreg[*]) has no direct measurement. Construction on 0.9: copy 128-bit slices into fresh qreg[128] targets with a permutation action (cx per wire, as EN ISA-6 measure_same), measure the copies, reset the collapsed source wire by wire via run-time slices and classical dispatch, then free. Capability kept; a direct qreg.split or wide measure is an efficiency candidate. Raised by the 0.9 draft job (b-isa-spec-so1), open question in spec/isa-0.9.PROGRESS.md.

title: ISA 0.8 §5.4/§10: token-to-region binding unstated
description: 0.8 mints a token per region (bennett_budget's region parameter) but never says whether a token validated for @p may be supplied to oracle_call @o. The §5.4 checks depend only on the object's layout. Draft 0.9 (spec/Bennett-ISA-Spec-0.9-draft.md §5.4, entry K3): a token MAY be supplied to any region call of the program. Found while drafting 0.9 (b-isa-spec-so1).

title: ISA 0.8 §16: empty data image requires a forbidden trailing space
description: §16.1 forbids trailing spaces but HEX admits the empty string and §16.2 requires dataline NAME SP HEX NL. A zero-size data image therefore has no legal spelling satisfying both. Proposed smallest wording: the mandatory separator space of a data line whose HEX is empty is the sole trailing-space exception. Suite F accepts data symbol size 0 with NAME SP LF, rejects two spaces and rejects size mismatch. No existing §16.3 bytes change apart from a later full-version bump. Reported in ISA 0.9 evidence note; no spec edit.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: wording-only — allow exactly the required separator space on an empty-HEX data line; preserve zero-sized data capability. Suite F accepts NAME SP LF and rejects double space/size mismatch. No existing vector changes. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: G-15: Oracle payloads wider than 128 bits
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2b (G-15).

Verdict: New candidate gap.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §3.3 'iN (1 <= N <= 128)'; `lift.retval v` is the only write of result_val; casts produce iM <= 128.

Blocks: Blocks no rung; workaround is one oracle computation per 128-bit output slice (recompute k times).

Change: `lift.retval` over several locations into slices of tgt, or a region-valued target.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — k equal-fault-prefix slice calls sharing caller-owned fr, plus one zero-payload call for even k, yield exactly one fault XOR without private fault cleanup. Exhausted/successful two-slice construction checked on 2048 full tuples. No scalar-predicate rung blocker. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: G-14: Predicated step machine in quantum actions
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2b (G-14).

Verdict: New candidate gap.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §5.3 action body: 'gates; qcopy ... qpred qunpred qif qloop; oracle_call action_call ...', with no qjump/qbranch; `qloop ... while` needs 'cond : wire[n] ... computed before the loop from wires the body does not modify'.

Blocks: Blocks no rung; NS §4.2 'A quantum action whose body contains coherent internal control is, by definition, its bounded padded unitary' for unstructured CFGs and self-dependent loops (dialect TDL-10 works around it with history registers). Related: I2.

Change: step-machine rows in actions under the QCM injectivity and synchronisation conditions (NS §4.2, §7).
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — finite bounded gate/event expansions are expressible; arbitrary controller cleanup needs injectivity/synchronisation and cannot undo desired quantum gates with classical prefix reversal. General QCM lowering proof unverified; no demo rung needs a new action jump opcode. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: G-13: Interface-region base chosen at call time
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2b (G-13).

Verdict: New candidate gap.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §9.1 `"interface_regions": { "<oracle>": { "<region>": { "base" } } }` is static layout.

Blocks: Blocks no rung; the coherent arena of the taint-driven lifting (dialect TDL-4) must sit at one static base.

Change: a `mem` binding with a classical base argument, validated for disjointness at the call.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — static arena or logical-pointer-to-static-backing translation at each checked access realises the addressed case. Two translation rows per access after range selection; arbitrary mixed-heap generalisation unverified. No rung dependency. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-11: Host memory by reference at native addresses (launch argument)
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-11).

Verdict: Real gap for pointer-rich host data. Copy-in/copy-out of flat bytes works through hostcall. Pointers inside host structures cannot keep their values on the device, because CC memory cannot place an object at a host address.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §10: INT(width, bytes) to iN ..., F64 to f64, QREG to qreg[n] ..., TOKEN to token. 'Arguments and the entropy tape are copied'; hostcall copies [ptr, ptr+len) into a request and writes the reply. §7.1: CC memory consists of globals and a bump heap; there is no allocation at a chosen address.

Blocks: Blocks no rung (rungs run whole programs on the device). Blocks NS §3.3/§5 partial compilation over shared pointer-rich data. Dialect: D25, O-08.

Change: a launch argument kind `MEM(addr, len)`, or a CC `alloc.at addr n` within a host-window range of the layout.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — promote pointer-sharing bitcode callers to CC and preserve numerical pointers using the existing allocator. Direct mapping of an already-existing foreign native heap remains absent/unverified. No rung dependency; no incomplete alloc.at proposal accepted. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-8: R-tier fault propagation to the calling CC code; faulted run not reversible
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-8).

Verdict: Real gap. The ISA does not say what the CC caller of a faulted R call observes, and a FAILED run cannot be reversed even though §7.4 calls the faulted state 'reversed like any prefix'.

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §4.1 'R fault record'; §7.4 'fault record | cause code (§5.4) and location; terminal faulted state, reversed like any prefix'. §10 'Reverse eligibility: COMPLETED'.

Blocks: Blocks no rung (rungs 3/6 require fault-free runs).

Change: an R call returns a fault status to its CC caller, and runs ending in an R fault are reverse-eligible.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — exact proposal makes uncaught R faults terminal to the CC run and permits reversal of fully logged FAILED prefixes with no measurement/unverified release. No extra R result/status convention required. Fault-free rungs 3/6 unaffected. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-9: Borrowed wires outside static Q regions (borrowing driven from CC)
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-9).

Verdict: Real gap for borrowing driven from CC. Clean allocation is a sound semantic fallback (dialect D6).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §4.3: `qborrow` ... n wires in unknown state; usable only inside a borrow frame (§5.6). §4.8 lists qborrow under 'Q (actions)'; §9.4 callees qborrow only from the caller's designated idle set.

Blocks: Blocks no rung.

Change: allow qborrow/qreturn in CC with a borrow-frame discipline.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — a correct dirty-borrow user works with clean wires, or can use an existing verified Q borrow frame. Charge actual clean occupancy; do not claim dirty-rate savings for that fallback. No rung dependency. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-7: Fault code of a CC trap in launch results
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-7).

Verdict: Real gap (wording). No rule maps a CC trap cause to a §5.4 code. The only mapping given is §17 item 14 (unclean qreg.free -> FAULT_UB_TRAP).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §4.1 says only 'CC trap' (udiv, load, trap, ...); §10 'Fault records are read by bennett_result_nfaults / bennett_result_fault (codes of §5.4 ...)'.

Blocks: Blocks no rung. Also needed for the dialect's reversible-budget fault code (dialect issue 1.4-e).

Change: a table in ISA §4.1 from trap cause to §5.4 code (div0 -> 5, MIN/-1 -> 6, out-of-allocation -> 7, trap -> 4, alloc failure -> 2), and a CC/R `fault C` instruction so dialect-level traps (budget, T-*) report their own code.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — specify CC/R trap cause mapping and explicit fault C, with frame/reversal and launch result rules. R step counters already exist; exact exhaustion code1 uses this instruction. Code10 may describe virtualised coherent entropy. See also zero-cause defect b-isa-spec-7qu. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-5: Two simultaneous slices of one qreg
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-5).

Verdict: Real gap (efficiency). Workarounds in 0.8: one `qreg[1]` per wire with static dispatch (O(n^2) for gate2, O(n^3) for gate3, static widths only); or a quantum-addressed gate in an action (index materialised into wires by an oracle with args, then `qpred (a==k)` per k: O(n) gates).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §3.3: `q2 = qreg.slice q lo len` ... q viewed; q2 MUST be the operand of exactly one region call and of nothing else ... any use of q while viewed is ill-formed. Indexed operand `w[i]` (literal i).

Blocks: Blocks no rung.

Change: `qreg.slices q (lo_1,len_1) ... (lo_k,len_k)` producing disjoint views consumed by one region call.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: efficiency — one joint-parent action accesses both indexed wires without simultaneous views; runtime indices dispatch to static actions. Proposed slice wording restores VIEWED pre-state on inverse call and LIVE parent on inverse slice. No rung dependency. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-4: qreg of run-time width; qreg values in memory or tables
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-4).

Verdict: Real gap. Blocks run-time-sized registers and handle collections whose size is known only at run time (NS §3.1 handle tables, §4.1/§4.2 dynamic allocation; Bennett.jl's vectors of qubits).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §3.3: `qreg[n]` is a type with literal n; `q = qreg.new cls n`. §3.2: handles live only in the 'classical environment'; classical memory is 'byte-addressed'. §4.1 has no instruction that stores, loads or converts a qreg. §10 binds `QREG` to `qreg[n]` with the register's n.

Blocks: Blocks no rung if rung 4's register width is a build-time constant. Dialect issues: B-07, B-24.

Change: `qreg[*]` with run-time n, plus either qreg storable in CC memory as an opaque id (`qreg.id` / `qreg.from_id`, the latter trapping on stale ids) or a CC register table `qtab.get/set`.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — dynamic qreg[*], width/id/from_id and shared alias ledger specify uniform dynamic widths and ordinary handle-table lookup. Static register files already work; unbounded instance count alone is not an impossibility proof because recursion retains registers. No fixed-width demo rung blocker. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

title: ISA-3: qinplace has no ins / mem / args operands
description:
Source: bennett-dialect-spec/docs/audit/2026-10-29-dialect-0.1-narrowing-audit.md section 2 (ISA-3).

Verdict: Real gap for `qinplace`. Writing the macro out by hand in an action does not substitute, because §6.2 binds every cleanup to 'its exact computing sequence' (reverse or recompute, §6.4) and the `ginv` call that cleans `t` is neither. Oracle args are NOT a gap (ISA §4.7, §5.1, §9.1); the JCS spelling of types in `"args"` is an editorial item (use the §16.2 type spelling as JCS strings).

ISA 0.8 evidence quoted by the audit: ISA §4.5: `qinplace @g @ginv tk x` ... Sem: `t = qalloc any n; f = qalloc any F; oracle_call @g tk (x) t f; qexch x t; oracle_call @ginv tk (x) t f; qfree t; qfree f` has no ins, mem or args. By contrast §4.7 `oracle_call @o tk (ins..) tgt fr (mem..) (args..)`, §5.1 `(args n: i64)`, §9.1 `"args":[types]`.

Blocks: Blocks no rung; blocks NS §3.1/§4.2 parametrised in-place updates (`x += a` with run-time a, controlled modular multiplication by a run-time constant). Dialect issue: 1.4-f.

Change: `qinplace @g @ginv tk x (ins..) (mem..) (args..)`, the §4.5 macro passing them to both oracle_calls; §6.1 transfer `x: perm with S_x U ins U cells U Pi`.
notes: [isa09-evidence 2026-10-29] Verdict: gap — extend certified qinplace to ins/mem/args, state inverse-pair cleanup exception and parameter/version provenance. Explicit compute/swap/inverse-call is not automatically an exact-sequence cleanup. Finite synthesis/library bijections exist; no demo rung requires the general declared-pair contract. Evidence: docs/notes/2026-10-29-isa-09-evidence.md.

description:
